title: Ang 659: Bhikhan
tomorrow: the groom is scared at 5 a.m. who's he supposed to tell?

cards: Cough syrup tastes like a dare. Ginger tea burns on the way down. Plain water, when you're really sick, can taste like the best thing in the world.
On ang 659, the bhagat Bhikhan answers yesterday's question. His body is giving out, and the medicine he asks for is the Name, which he pictures as pure, sweet water.

teach.b: Bhikhan's hymns in Sorath close the raga. The first is honest about old age, in paraphrase: my eyes run with water, my body has grown weak, my hair has turned white as milk. My throat is choked; I can't get a word out.
What can a person do now? Then he turns.
O Lord, be my physician, and save your devotee. Notice he doesn't pretend. The list is plain and physical: eyes, hair, throat.
He doesn't call the body unimportant. He describes it failing, in detail, and then asks for help from the one he trusts. And the help has a taste.

Bhikhan calls the Lord's Name pure, nectar-like water, the medicine, by the Guru's grace. Medicine is something you take in, a little at a time, not something you think about. Here's what the hymn doesn't say.

teach.h: IT NEVER SAYS SKIP THE DOCTOR.
teach.b: It never tells anyone to skip a doctor or stop caring for the body.
It asks God to be the physician of the whole person, the one who stays when the voice gives out.
And it's worth noticing: one of the last voices in raga Sorath is an old man who can barely speak, and his hymn is kept in the Granth for everyone to sing.

how: Bhikhan's hymns are read with the other bhagats' at the end of raga Sorath in the Guru Granth Sahib; Sikhs often speak of the Name as a medicine, a healing for the whole person.

s: Bhikhan's hymn tells the sick to skip doctors and only pray
it never says that. it asks God to be the physician of the whole person.
Bhikhan describes his aging body in plain, physical detail
eyes, hair, a choked throat that can't get a word out.
they close it, after Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas.

games.q: your grandmother has a bad cough and says, 'the Name is my medicine.' your aunt worries that means she won't see a doctor. what fits Bhikhan?
o: both can be true; the hymn asks God to heal the whole person and never says skip care.
she's right to skip the doctor; the hymn says the Name is the only medicine.
your aunt is right; a hymn about medicine can't mean anything real.
games.why: Bhikhan names the body's failing honestly and asks the Lord to be his physician. the text is silent about doctors; it doesn't forbid them.

practice: Pour a small glass of plain water. Take one slow sip and hold it in your mouth a moment before you swallow, noticing its cool, its taste, the way it goes down. Sip again, slowly, a few times through the sit, as if it were medicine.
